components.name: Entity Reference
components.description: A tinted name with a dotted underline; the hover card always names the type.

narrative.overview: Wyrd is read, not watched. The screen is a lit page in a dark room: near-black paper, bone-coloured ink, one lantern hue, and thin ruled lines instead of boxes. The story takes the reading column; every piece of machinery — the status strip, rolls, clocks, key hints, item metadata — takes the monospace chrome column. That split is the identity.
keyCharacteristics: One campaign hue, three fixed signal accents, zero decorative colour.
A reading-font slot and a monospace chrome slot; the roles never swap.
1px rules and flat surfaces; no shadows, glass or glow.
A 660px reading column with margin notes as annotations, not a sidebar.
44px targets, keyboard-first hints, and text that stays above WCAG AA.

rules.name: The One Lantern Rule
rules.body: A campaign has exactly one hue. It is the only variable colour on the screen; adding a second accent is a redesign, not a customisation.

rules.name: The Signal Trio Rule
rules.body: Gold means companion or item, red means danger or canon, cyan means link or faction. Never reassign a signal to make a layout prettier.

rules.name: The Type Is Named Rule
rules.body: Entity tint is never the only cue. Every reference also carries a type in its card and a dotted underline, so a player who cannot distinguish the hues still knows what they are looking at.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Story text uses the reading slot; every number, key, clock, roll and label uses the chrome slot. Never set body prose in monospace, and never set a roll result in the serif.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change — level, roll, clock segment, time, HP, currency — uses tabular figures. Proportional figures make a living character sheet twitch.

rules.name: The 66-Character Rule
rules.body: Reader prose is 660px wide — about 66 characters at 20px. Never full-bleed the story to gain density; density belongs to Cockpit.

rules.name: The Fixed Chrome Rule
rules.body: The status strip and hotbar are fixed chrome. The story scrolls between them; the page does not scroll the chrome out of reach.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: If an element needs to separate, use a rule, a lightness step or spacing. A box-shadow is a bug in this system.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no frosted panels, no gradient text. “Lantern Glass” is a flat true-black preset, not a glassmorphism theme.

rules.name: The One Border Rule
rules.body: One 1px rule per division. A filled surface does not also get a border; a bordered surface does not also get a shadow.

dos: Do keep exactly one campaign hue and the three fixed signals; put the hue in --hue and use var(--accent).
Do keep prose at 660px in Reader and 20px/1.7; let Cockpit carry the density.
Do use 1px rules, lightness steps and spacing for separation; there is no shadow.
Do give every interactive element a 44px target, a visible hover state and a 2px hue focus ring.
Do use tabular figures for every changing number and monospace for every piece of chrome.
Do theme selection, caret, scrollbars and focus rings from the palette; they are part of the screen.
Do print the entity type in every reference card and keep the dotted underline, so colour is never the only cue.
donts: Don’t add a second accent, a gradient, a glow or a coloured halo.
Don’t use Ari Gold for danger or Canon Red for a companion; the signals are fixed.
Don’t use hue as decoration on large fills; it is a line, a numeral, a word or a focus ring.
Don’t put a card inside a card, or a shadow on a bordered surface.
Don’t round Reader or Cockpit cards; the book page is square.
Don’t set long prose in monospace or rolls in the serif.
Don’t make a menu hint the only label for a control.
